kinds.one_liner: Where a river runs out into a lake.

why_fish_gather.text: Fish that live in the lake pass through here to feed or to run upstream. The river also carries food out into open water.
why_fish_gather.label: General reasoning, not a record about this spot

kinds.one_liner: Two streams meeting. Different temperature, speed and food mix at the join.

why_fish_gather.text: Two flows mixing makes a seam between fast and slow water, which fish use for shelter with food drifting past. A creek that runs cooler than the river can also give fish a place to ease out of warm water.
why_fish_gather.label: General reasoning, not a record about this spot

kinds.one_liner: The water just downstream of a dam or weir.

why_fish_gather.text: A dam or weir blocks fish from moving further upstream, so they gather in the water just below it. That water is churned up and rich in oxygen.
why_fish_gather.label: General reasoning, not a record about this spot

kinds.one_liner: Places that volunteer mappers have marked as set aside for fishing.

why_fish_gather.text: Someone has mapped this as a place to fish, usually because the water is easy and allowed to reach. That is about access, so it says nothing by itself about what is swimming there.
why_fish_gather.label: General reasoning, not a record about this spot

kinds.one_liner: Reaches with few public observation records, which may mean few anglers or just few observers.

why_fish_gather.text: These reaches have few public observation records. That can mean fewer anglers, few observers or hard access, and it never tells you whether fish are there.
why_fish_gather.label: General reasoning, not a record about this spot

terms.definition: A stream junction is the place where two streams meet and become one.

terms.plain: Where a river meets a lake
terms.definition: A river mouth is where a river or creek flows out into a lake.

terms.plain: A wall holding back a river
terms.definition: A dam is a wall built across a river to hold water back. It usually forms a pond or reservoir above it.

terms.plain: A low wall across a river
terms.definition: A weir is a low wall built across a river that water flows over. It holds the water back a little.

terms.plain: The water just below a dam
terms.definition: The water below a dam is the part of a river just downstream of it.

terms.plain: A stream running through a pipe under a road
terms.definition: A culvert is a pipe or box channel that carries a stream under a road, trail or railway.
terms.mapped_from: Ontario government water map and OpenStreetMap (barriers)

terms.plain: Where a stream flows into a lake
terms.definition: An inlet is a place where a stream flows into a lake.

terms.plain: Where a stream leaves a lake
terms.definition: An outlet is a place where a stream starts at a lake and flows away.
An island is land surrounded on all sides by water.

terms.plain: Land reaching out into the water
terms.definition: A point is a narrow piece of shore that sticks out into a lake.

terms.plain: A long arm of land reaching into the water
terms.definition: A peninsula is land with water on most sides, joined to the shore at one end.

terms.plain: Where the bottom gets deep quickly
terms.definition: A drop-off is a place where the bottom of a lake or river slopes steeply from shallow to deep water.
terms.mapped_from: Ontario government lake depth surveys (depth contours)

terms.plain: A shallow rise in the lake bottom
terms.definition: A hump is a place where the bottom of a lake rises to shallower water than the water around it.
terms.mapped_from: Ontario government lake depth surveys (depth contours)

terms.plain: A walkway built out over the water
terms.definition: A pier is a structure built out from the shore over the water.

terms.plain: A wall of rock or concrete built to block waves
terms.definition: A breakwater is a wall of rock or concrete built in the water to shelter a shore or harbour from waves.

terms.plain: Sheltered water where boats are kept
terms.definition: A harbour is a sheltered area of water where boats are moored or launched.

terms.plain: The edge of a weed bed
terms.definition: A weed edge is the boundary between a bed of underwater plants and open water.

Barometric pressure is the weight of the air above a place, measured in hectopascals (hPa). It rises and falls as weather systems pass, so the direction it is moving says which way the weather is heading.
